1553268835263942656.a: Dumbest thing I'm glad programmers are growing out of is using SQL to store data. You can only query/search a SQL database. If you already know what data you need then why do you query? Rather than try to rebuild the world at retrieval time update named objects when they change.

1553268836421570560.a: That is, its faster to load an object in S3 as JSON than it is to load the data from SQL, figure out which bits of data go where, create an object in memory, copy that out to JSON. Do all that stuff at WRITE time not read. You have an eternity to write things. No time to read. ✌️

1553270421264502784.a: Using SQL as a primary data store feels like taking your car apart into thousands of pieces when you go home from work at night. Then frantically putting it back together 10 minutes before you need to be at work. Your whole life becomes slave to this thing you don't even use.

1553271588371431424.a: background: I ported search engines in the 90s. From my perspective, SQL is basically a search engine for a database. Like MySQL isn't an SQL database. It's a SQL search engine for MyISAM or similar databases. You almost always know enough in a web request to not need to search.
